Overview

Rebuilding a nation's visual identity
for a new era.

The Syrian Arab Republic stands at a profound turning point — and its visual presence needed to reflect that transformation. This wasn't a graphic refresh. It was a complete reimagining of national symbolism through a contemporary visual language that honors thousands of years of history while looking firmly toward the future.

The work began with deep research into Syria's cultural heritage — the architecture of Damascus, the craftsmanship of Aleppo, and the symbolism of the Eagle of Saladin — to form a complete visual system that speaks of belonging, sovereignty, and resilience.

Application — Passport

A travel document
that carries identity.

The new Syrian passport merges security, aesthetics, and national symbolism. Every detail — from the golden eagle embossed on forest green, to the typographic hierarchy — reflects a state that is confident in its heritage and clear in its future direction.

Syrian Arab Republic — Official Passport / New Design System 02
Ajami Pattern System

A visual anchor
rooted in Damascus.

The Ajami pattern isn't ornamental filler — it's a visual anchor that brings depth and cultural continuity to the identity. Inspired by the decorative art form found in historical Damascene palaces and heritage homes.

Challenge

Heritage and modernity — simultaneously.

The real challenge wasn't design — it was balance. How do you build an identity that respects thousands of years of history while reflecting a state looking toward the future? We had to avoid a modernity that severs roots, and a conservatism that freezes the image in the past.

Solution

A living visual system that scales across every application.

We began with a deep study of Syrian national symbols. The Eagle of Saladin was redrawn in a contemporary language — preserving its symbolic values while breathing new life into them. The color system draws from Syria's natural landscape: the green of Ghouta, the gold of wheat, and the depth of black basalt.

Color System

Colors drawn from
Syria's natural memory.

Forest, wheat, basalt, olive — every color in the system has a story rooted in the Syrian landscape and cultural heritage.

Visual Research

Architecture,
nature, symbolism.

Every element in the identity is traceable to a real cultural reference — the black basalt of Syrian architecture, the golden eagle in its natural form, the geometry of historic domes.

"
Simplicity isn't a style — it's a decision. And in every element of this identity, there is a conscious choice to let go of what doesn't serve the message.
Mohanned Al Rahmah — Design Director

🏅 Presidential Recognition

Honored by the President
of the Syrian Arab Republic.

It was a profound honor to be received by His Excellency, President Ahmad Al-Shar'a, in a special recognition ceremony held to honor the creative team behind the development of the country's official visual identity. The meeting reflected the deep national appreciation for the efforts invested in shaping a design that embodies Syria's heritage, sovereignty, and renewed institutional presence.
